To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cep63 is a novel Cdk1-binding protein that is recruited to centrosomes and that is essential for the activation of Cdk in mitotic cells.

(i) Human Cep63 binds and recruits Cdk-1 to centrosome, (ii) Cep63 depletion induces centrosome ampliﬁcation and polyploidization, (iii) Cep63 over-expression induces centrosome duplication during interphase, (iv) Cep63 mRNA is up-regulated in neuroblastoma cases with MYCN ampliﬁcations.
Cep63 recruits Ccd1 to the centriole and that Cep63 over-expression induces centrosome amplifications and polyploidisation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the regulation of mitotic spindle formation, a process that is frequently deregulated in cancer, and with the mechanisms of centrosome ampliﬁcation, which is a hallmark of cancer cells and a potential source of genomic instability.
the molecular and cellular biology of the centrosome, a microtubule organizing centre (MTOC), which is essential for cell division.
understanding the molecular basis of mitotic spindle assembly, centrosome function and cell-cycle control in human cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Cep63 is a novel centrosomal Cdc2/Cdk1 recruitment factor that is essential for centrosome-mediated mitotic entry and for genome maintenance, and whose deregulation may be involved in the pathogenesis of cancer.
the centrosomal Cep63 protein is essential for mitosis, and that it recruits Cdk1 from the cytoplasm to centrosomes.
the Cep63 protein is a centrosomal Cdc2 kinase recruiter that is essential for the initiation of mitosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cep63 is a novel centrosomal protein with a dual role in mitosis.
Cep63 is an essential component of the centrosome that recruits Cdk1, thereby regulating mitotic entry.
Cep63 is a new regulator of mitosis, and that Cep63 over-expression is associated with cancer progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cep63 functions as a Cdk1 recruitment factor to centrosomes that is essential for cell-cycle progression.
centrosomes are not only important organizers of the mitosis but also play a role in the regulation of mitotic onset.
Cep63 is a novel component of the human centromere that is essential for centrosome duplication and mitotic entry.
